notes:
Opportunity: Timberline Capacity Labs evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private for control-plane and edge inference across their manufacturing lines. Primary negotiation focus: SLA uptime %, credit schedule, maintenance windows, and P1/P2 support response.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-01-28: Intro call (AE Maya) — high-level requirements, interested in dedicated GPU pools, VPC.
- 2026-02-10: Architecture deep-dive (SE Liam) — confirmed on-prem feasibility, initial reserved GPU sizing: 8x A100-eq for peak (burstable), baseline 4 nodes.
- 2026-02-24: Security questionnaire returned (SOC2 in-scope), requested KMS + audit logging details. Drive: SLA_Draft_v1 attached.
- 2026-03-01: POC kickoff (private deployment) — 3-week run to validate latency SLO and failover behavior. Fireflies ff-20260301-7b2d9a.
- 2026-03-04: Load test results uploaded (attached) — sustained throughput ~220 req/s, p95 latency 85ms, p99 latency 230ms under current config.
- 2026-03-05: SLA negotiation meeting (AE/SE/Legal + Timberline procurement) — Redwood proposed default hosted SLA (99.95% uptime; credit tiers: 5%/<99.95, 15%/<99.9; max credits 50%). Timberline pushing for 99.99 and steeper credits to match cost impact.

Use-case & technical requirements (short):
- Workloads: operator-assistant chat (low latency), real-time control inference (hard SLO), embeddings for anomaly detection, reranking for sensor event triage.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 100ms for short chat/control requests; p99 target < 200ms during steady state.
- Throughput: baseline 150-250 req/s; peak bursts up to 400 req/s for 10-30s intervals.
- KV/prefix caching required to meet tail latency. Prefers per-customer dedicated cache nodes.
- Reserved GPU planning: want guaranteed baseline 4 GPU-equivalent nodes with ability to burst to 8 for peak windows. Autoscale policy must be predictable and bounded.

SLA negotiation points captured:
- Uptime target: Timberline requests 99.99% for Dedicated plan; Redwood current offer 99.95 for Dedicated. Timberline argues cost impact of downtime (manufacturing line halt) justifies tighter SLA.
- Credit schedule: Timberline wants credits proportionate to revenue impact (tiered: 10% for 99.95-99.99, 25% for 99.9-99.95, 50% below 99.9) and explicit monthly cap aligned to ARR. Redwood's legal wants a simple % credit model with max cap at 50%.
- Maintenance windows: Timberline requires no more than 2 scheduled full-cluster maintenance events per year for on-prem/private, with scheduled windows in local off-shift hours (00:00-05:00 local). Emergency maint must have 2-hour notice whenever possible.
- Support SLAs: Timberline requests P1 response <= 30 minutes and mitigation plan within 2 hours; Redwood standard support target currently P1 < 1 hour initial response and 4-hour mitigation. Timberline wants 24/7 phone escalation path and named on-call for critical incidents.
- Fault isolation & fallback: asks that Redwood include automatic fallback to cold standby nodes and explicit runbook for failover with RTO < 15 minutes for critical models.
- Availability measurement: Timberline requests access to token-level uptime/latency logs and monthly attestation; retention at least 12 months for audits.

Open items / blockers:
- Legal redline on credit schedule and cap (Timberline legal vs Redwood legal)
- Maintenance frequency acceptance for Private deployment (internal ops constraints at Timberline)
- Exact reserved GPU instance types and pricing bands for guaranteed baseline vs burst capacity.

Stated quotes from procurement:
- "If our lines stop, every minute costs us six figures. We need SLA terms that translate to that risk." — Timberline procurement lead.
- "We can accept a modest premium for tighter SLOs, but credits must reflect operational impact, not just a flat rebate." — CTO.
